title: Inspecting and fitting harnesses and lanyards
audience: Workers who wear or check harnesses and lanyards on trade and exterior jobs, and their supervisors.
learningOutcomes: Carry out a before-use check covering a harness and a lanyard, covering webbing, stitching, buckles, connectors and energy absorbers.
Decide whether an item must be withdrawn from service, and say why.
Fit a harness correctly and have the fit checked by a second person.
Record the item identity, the in-service date and each inspection in a log.

instruction.heading: Inspection is the everyday check that matters most
instruction.body: A harness or lanyard that looks sound on the outside can still fail under load. The sources agree that an item should be inspected before each use and again afterwards, and that a competent individual should examine it at set intervals. An item that has taken a fall or an impact load comes out of service at once, even if it looks undamaged. This lesson teaches the worker's own check. It does not replace a periodic examination by a competent individual, and completing the lesson does not make the worker that person.

instruction.heading: Work through the item in the same order every time
instruction.body: Use a fixed order so nothing is skipped. For webbing, look for cuts, tears, fraying, abrasion, discolouration, heat marks and stiffness that suggests chemical contact, and run the strap through your hands to feel for hard spots and stretching. Stitching that carries the load is often in a different colour; any stitch that is missing, cut, frayed or incomplete is a reason to withdraw the item. For buckles and adjusters, look for distortion, sharp edges, cracks and corrosion, and operate each one to confirm it locks and releases. For connectors, check the body and the gate for distortion, cracks and corrosion, and confirm the gate closes and locks fully. For the energy absorber, check that the two ends of its cover are sealed and undamaged, with no cuts, tears or heat damage, and that it has not opened.

instruction.heading: The lanyard needs its own check
instruction.body: Inspect the full length of the lanyard, including each end, each splice or stitched join, and any shock-absorbing pack. Confirm the length matches the length used in the clearance calculation. A lanyard that has been shortened, knotted or joined with a connector that is not approved for it must be withdrawn. A lanyard used for fall arrest must never be relied on for positioning or for hauling materials.

instruction.heading: Protect the equipment in use
instruction.body: Keep lanyards away from sharp edges and abrasive surfaces, and use edge protectors where a lanyard runs over a corner. A lanyard that is cut or abraded is unsafe. Store equipment away from heat, sunlight and chemicals, and keep records so that every item can be traced.

instruction.heading: Fitting the harness
instruction.body: Fit the harness before you go up, then check the fit after you have connected. Put the harness on properly rather than stepping into it on the ground, which wets and dirties it and can expose it to chemicals. Fit the leg straps first, then the chest strap, and keep the back attachment point high on the rear of the harness. A slack harness can injure the skin and body during a fall, so tighten it until it fits closely. Have a second person check the fit, including the straps and buckle positions, before the worker goes up.

instruction.heading: When an item must come out of service
instruction.body: Remove an item from service at once if it shows any of the following: a cut or tear in the webbing; a missing or broken stitch; a distorted or cracked connector; a buckle that does not lock; an energy absorber that has opened, or has been exposed to heat or chemicals; or any impact load from a fall. Tag the item, store it apart from usable equipment, and tell the supervisor. Only a competent individual may decide whether an item that has taken a load can return to service, and the item stays out of use until that decision is recorded.

instruction.heading: Life, storage and records
instruction.body: Clean equipment with the method the maker recommends and let it dry in the shade rather than in direct sunlight. A non-Australian source gives a service life and a shelf life; those figures are not used here. Record the in-service date, the serial or item number, each inspection, and the date of any withdrawal.

procedure: Lay the harness flat and inspect the webbing on both faces and along the edges.
Check each stitch line, including the stitching at the attachment point.
Operate each buckle and adjuster to confirm it locks and releases.
Inspect each connector for distortion, cracks, corrosion and gate function.
Inspect the lanyard and energy absorber along their full length.
Record the result in the log, and withdraw the item if any criterion is failed.
Fit the harness, then have a second person check the fit.
After any use, repeat the inspection and record any impact or exposure.

workedExamples.situation: A worker finds a short, pale, fraying patch on one shoulder strap of a harness on the morning of a job.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the harness be used for the day?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Fraying and abrasion are reasons to withdraw an item. The worker tells the supervisor, tags the harness and uses a spare that has passed its inspection. The job starts only once the spare is checked.

workedExamples.situation: After a short fall into a harness the previous week, the energy absorber cover looks sealed but has a faint crease along one side.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Has the item been used safely, and what happens to it now?
workedExamples.reasoning: An arrested fall means the item is withdrawn regardless of its appearance, because the energy absorber may have deployed. The item is tagged and removed, the supervisor is told, the event is recorded, and a competent individual decides whether it can return to service.

equipmentAndPpe: Edge protectors or sleeves for lanyards at corners

commonErrors.error: Inspecting only the outside of the webbing.
commonErrors.prevention: Turn the strap over, check both faces and the edges, and check the stitching.

commonErrors.error: Drying a harness in direct sunlight.
commonErrors.prevention: Air dry in the shade, away from heat.

commonErrors.error: Dropping the harness on the floor and climbing into it.
commonErrors.prevention: Put it on properly, one arm at a time, and have it checked.

commonErrors.error: Keeping an item that has arrested a fall because it looks undamaged.
commonErrors.prevention: Any arrested fall means withdrawal until a competent individual has cleared the item.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Warning: an item that has taken a fall or impact load must stay out of use until a competent individual has inspected it and recorded a decision.
Warning: do not use an item with any cut, tear, missing stitch, distorted connector or failed locking device.
Set the interval from the manufacturer's instructions and the business's approved procedure.
Licence notice: only a competent individual may decide whether a loaded item can return to service. Completing this lesson does not make a worker that person and does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Each inspection criterion is checked and recorded.
Withdrawn items are tagged and stored apart from usable equipment.
The fit is checked by a second person before the worker goes up.
documentationEvidence: Pre-use inspection log entry with item ID, date and result
summary: Inspect in a fixed order before and after every use.
Withdraw any item with a fault, and any item that has arrested a fall.
A harness is fitted and then checked; it is not thrown on and stepped into.
Only a competent individual may return a loaded item to service.

knowledgeChecks.question: A harness has a frayed patch on a strap, but the patch is short and the strap still feels firm. What is the right action?
options: Use it for the rest of the job, since it feels firm
Withdraw it from service and tell the supervisor.
Use it only for positioning and not for falls
Wash it and use it again once it is dry again

knowledgeChecks.question: Which items must be withdrawn from use after a fall has been arrested?
options: Only the connector, which is the part that usually fails first and the anchor is checked later
The whole system involved, until a competent individual has decided whether it can return to service.
Nothing, if the worker is unhurt and the harness looks fine and the crew is happy with it
Only the anchor point, which is the single part most often damaged and the anchor is rechecked next week

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should the back attachment point on a harness sit when the harness is fitted?
options: At the waist, to keep the lanyard low.
High on the back, centred over the spine.
On the chest, where it is visible.
At the hip on one side.

knowledgeChecks.question: When should a harness or lanyard be inspected, according to the lesson?
options: Before each use and again afterwards
